correctness.rationale: The frozen mathematics is correct; the replacement was rechecked on the narrowed claim. IID continuous priorities induce a uniform permutation on the 30 labeled edges. Conditional on any ordered accepted prefix, the order of still-available edges is uniform by exchangeability: each was available throughout that prefix, so swapping their order preserves the event. Thus the exact free-set recurrence chooses the next available edge uniformly and then deletes its endpoints, and the matching-prefix recurrence follows by partitioning the event by the last accepted edge. The unassigned-vertex matching enumeration is exhaustive and unique because a matching prescribes the first unassigned vertex's partner or unmatched status. The terminal independent-unmatched-set test is exactly maximality. A separate exact replay reproduced the five credited kinetic fractions and all five maximal-matching counts (5,420,2280,1040,36), totaling 3,781. The resulting uniform cumulative counts are 5,425,2705,3745 divided by 3,781. Subtracting the greedy CDF gives the four positive fractions in the replacement, and the perfect-output ratio 155312512865429/20011992000000 is correct. Outside the nontrivial thresholds the two CDFs agree. The replacement retains these facts and uses, rather than newly asserts, the duplicate kinetic law.
residual_risks: The reproduced exact probabilities concern a uniform edge order and one finite graph; no transient or physical kinetics, or general dominance across graphs, is established.
